A person should understand why another feature helps them—and choose whether to cross into it.

“I came here to teach. Why would I volunteer?”
START WITH A REAL PERSON
Their current role, goal and reason to consider a second service.
MAKE THE HANDOFF USEFUL
A relevant invitation, consent and a clear next action—not just a menu link.
SHOW VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Explain what the person gains and what the recipient or service gains.
15 proposed bridges · 2 complete journeys · role boundaries · implementation priorities

PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
Teacher’s reason
“I want to use my Quran expertise to support someone beyond a scheduled class.”
Bridge experience
Invite the teacher to offer Quran support; reuse consented expertise and complete volunteer checks.
Seeker’s reason
“This approved volunteer is also an approved Quran teacher. I can see why the match is relevant.”
DOES EVERY TEACHER NEED VOLUNTEERING?
No. It becomes relevant when they choose to offer support.
WHAT DOES THE TEACHER BADGE MEAN?
Relevant approved expertise—not guaranteed safety or automatic case access.

YES—WHEN THERE IS A REAL REASON
A teacher wants to contribute; a volunteer needs preparation; a seeker asks for learning help.
NO—WHEN THE SECOND SERVICE ADDS NO VALUE
A teacher only wants to teach; a reader only wants Quran; a seeker needs immediate practical help.
Relevant invitation

PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 01 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A teacher can turn expertise into relevant care
Learning centre → Volunteer support  |  An approved Quran teacher
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“I teach Quran. I would also like to help someone who needs personal guidance.”
USE WHEN
Offer volunteering when the teacher wants to give support beyond scheduled classes.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
A teacher may only publish and teach. Volunteering stays optional.
Teaching profile
Approved topics and languages establish relevant expertise.
Choose to help
An invitation offers Quran-related support; the teacher opts in.
Volunteer approval
MRM checks suitability, training, capacity and case boundaries.
Relevant support match
The seeker sees approved teaching credentials and accepts the offer.
CARRY FORWARD
With consent: approved teacher status, verified subject, languages and public profile.
KEEP SEPARATE
Teacher payment does not buy case access. No private student records are shared.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
The seeker can judge relevant expertise; the teacher gains a meaningful way to serve. Credentials support confidence, not a guarantee of safety.
SUCCESS: Eligible teachers opting in → approved volunteers → accepted subject-relevant matches.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 02 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A volunteer can learn before accepting a new task
Volunteer support → Learning centre  |  A volunteer offered unfamiliar work
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“I want to help, but I need preparation for this kind of support.”
USE WHEN
Recommend an approved course when a real duty requires a skill or refresher.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Existing qualified volunteers do not repeat irrelevant classes; no blanket course requirement.
Readiness gap
The volunteer or coordinator identifies a specific skill gap.
Relevant training
Open the approved course with topic and required outcome explained.
Learning evidence
Record completion; assess readiness separately where needed.
Return to duty
MRM updates eligibility and offers suitable work after approval.
CARRY FORWARD
Course reference, completion and separately assessed competencies, with appropriate visibility.
KEEP SEPARATE
Completion alone is not volunteer approval. Private learning notes stay private.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Volunteers get practical preparation; seekers receive help from people approved for the task.
SUCCESS: Training completion → assessed readiness → eligible task acceptance; monitor support quality.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 03 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A support conversation can open the right learning path
Support requests → Learning centre  |  A seeker asking for Quran-reading help
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“I need a patient beginner class, in my language, at a time I can attend.”
USE WHEN
Suggest a class when learning addresses the person’s expressed need and they want it.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Urgent welfare support continues independently. No class enrolment is required for aid.
Expressed need
The assigned helper asks whether learning support would be useful.
Consent to refer
The seeker selects a goal, language and availability to share.
Suitable programme
Show approved beginner classes and relevant teacher credentials.
Optional enrolment
The seeker joins; the helper sees only the agreed referral status.
CARRY FORWARD
Chosen learning goal, language, availability and referral ID; share only what is needed.
KEEP SEPARATE
No full case narrative, financial circumstances or private chat enters a teacher profile.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
The seeker receives a practical next step; teachers reach learners who want the programme.
SUCCESS: Consented referrals → suitable enrolments → attendance and seeker-reported usefulness.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 04 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A Quran reader can find help for a specific learning goal
Quran utility → Learning centre  |  A person using Quran reading tools
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“I can read this passage, but I want help with pronunciation or meaning.”
USE WHEN
Offer a discreet learning action after the person explicitly asks for help on a topic.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Reading alone remains complete. Do not infer poor skill or send unsolicited judgments.
Ask for guidance
The reader chooses Learn this topic or Get reading help.
Choose learning goal
They select beginner reading, recitation or an approved topic.
Relevant discovery
Show approved teachers or programmes matching language and level.
Return to practice
After learning, a saved link returns to the selected passage.
CARRY FORWARD
Only the user-selected passage, learning goal and preferred language.
KEEP SEPARATE
No private reading history or worship-tracker record is shared with a teacher.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Daily use can become purposeful learning; teachers receive clearer learner intent.
SUCCESS: User-initiated learning opens → relevant enrolments → return to chosen practice.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 05 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A learner can ask for continuity after a class
Learning centre → Mentoring  |  A learner who wants individual follow-up
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“The class helped. I would like someone to guide my next steps.”
USE WHEN
Offer mentoring after a learner requests ongoing guidance or a teacher offers approved capacity.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Class enrolment does not enrol a person into mentoring or open private messaging automatically.
Request follow-up
The learner chooses a goal after the programme.
Available mentor
Show approved mentors relevant to topic, language and permitted boundaries.
Mutual acceptance
The mentor has capacity; the learner agrees to contact and expectations.
Ongoing guidance
Open the authorised relationship and optional agreed check-ins.
CARRY FORWARD
Chosen programme, learning goal and agreed availability; selected progress only with consent.
KEEP SEPARATE
No automatic access to class rosters, aid cases or private worship records.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Learners gain continuity; mentors support people whose needs match their expertise.
SUCCESS: Follow-up requests → mutually accepted matches → useful agreed check-ins.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 06 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A mentor can refer needs beyond the teaching relationship
Mentoring → Support requests  |  A mentor hearing about a practical difficulty
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“This learner needs help that I am not authorised or qualified to provide.”
USE WHEN
Offer a supported referral when the person wants help outside the mentor’s remit.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
A mentor does not investigate welfare issues or browse existing private cases.
Recognise the limit
The mentor explains the relevant support route without promising an outcome.
Person chooses help
The learner opens or agrees to a minimal support referral.
MRM triage
Authorised staff assess urgency, eligibility and the appropriate response.
Bounded follow-up
The mentor sees only the referral status the person agreed to share.
CARRY FORWARD
Consent, chosen category, contact preference and minimum agreed context.
KEEP SEPARATE
No blanket case access. Safeguarding disclosures follow the approved escalation policy.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
The person reaches qualified help; the mentor can stay within a clear teaching role.
SUCCESS: Accepted referrals → triaged requests → completed handoffs without excess disclosure.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 07 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A learning event can invite a separate service role
Learning events → Volunteer duties  |  A Halaqa attendee or teacher
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“I am attending this event. Can I help with registration or accessibility?”
USE WHEN
Offer clearly defined event tasks when organisers need capacity and the person opts in.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Attending a class never creates a duty. An event helper does not gain case access.
Event participation
The person views an approved programme and its support needs.
Choose a duty
They select a suitable task, time window and required checks.
Coordinator confirms
Check eligibility and avoid conflict with the person’s class time.
Event service
Show a separate duty card, instructions and attendance confirmation.
CARRY FORWARD
Event ID, chosen slot, contact consent and role-specific eligibility.
KEEP SEPARATE
Class attendance and duty acceptance are separate records; no attendee list is exported.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Organisers gain willing capacity; participants have a specific, manageable way to contribute.
SUCCESS: Opt-in duty requests → conflict-free confirmations → completed event tasks.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 08 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
An inspiring post can lead to a relevant programme
Community updates → Learning centre  |  A reader interested in an approved topic
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“This article is useful. Where can I learn this with a teacher?”
USE WHEN
Attach a specific approved programme when it genuinely expands on the post.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Not every post needs a conversion. General announcements can stand alone.
Relevant approved post
An author explains a topic with a clear source and audience.
Purposeful invitation
Read programme details or Meet the teacher explains the next step.
Programme context
Open topic, level, language, date and access information.
Voluntary participation
The reader chooses enrolment and can return to the original post.
CARRY FORWARD
Post ID, topic and linked programme; aggregate referral attribution where agreed.
KEEP SEPARATE
No sensitive-case targeting, fabricated testimonials or automatic enrolment.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Readers can act on genuine interest; teachers reach an appropriate audience.
SUCCESS: Post-to-programme opens → relevant enrolments; monitor usefulness and opt-outs.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 09 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
Repeated support needs can shape better programmes
Support operations → Learning planning  |  An MRM programme coordinator
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“We repeatedly receive beginner-learning requests in a language with little capacity.”
USE WHEN
Use restricted aggregate demand to commission a programme for an evidenced gap.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Do not publish identifiable case examples or infer demand from a tiny sensitive group.
Aggregate need
Authorised staff group agreed categories, languages and waiting demand.
Plan a response
MRM chooses a topic and suitable approved teacher capacity.
Publish programme
Create a public description without beneficiary identities.
Measure the response
Track programme capacity, consented referrals and unmet demand.
CARRY FORWARD
Only approved aggregate demand, programme requirements and non-identifying outcomes.
KEEP SEPARATE
Case files and individual identities never enter a public programme brief.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Learning supply responds to real community needs; support teams gain a useful referral option.
SUCCESS: Demand gap → commissioned capacity → suitable referrals; review remaining unmet need.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 10 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A verified outcome can invite responsible participation
Service outcomes → Community updates  |  A beneficiary willing to share an experience
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“I want to thank the programme, but I want control over what people can see.”
USE WHEN
Publish a verified, consented story with an appropriate participation destination.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Assistance and recognition never depend on agreeing to publicity.
Separate invitation
After service, staff offer an optional story process with no effect on aid.
Specific consent
Agree wording, images, visibility and the withdrawal process.
Review and publish
Check accuracy, minimisation and moderation before publication.
Relevant invitation
Readers can discover a real class or apply to volunteer.
CARRY FORWARD
Only approved story assets and programme links under the documented consent.
KEEP SEPARATE
No case narrative, identity number or location is copied by default; no guaranteed outcomes.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
The storyteller controls disclosure; readers see credible reasons to participate.
SUCCESS: Consent compliance, correction requests and relevant participation; never reward forced stories.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 11 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A local utility can surface a genuinely useful gathering
Prayer / nearby places → Learning events  |  A person checking prayer times or a mosque
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“Is there an approved beginner Halaqa near this place?”
USE WHEN
Offer nearby programmes when the person requests local learning information.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Prayer times remain usable without events, location sharing or an account where supported.
Local intent
The person selects a mosque or manually chosen area.
Explore gatherings
A separate action requests approved programmes nearby.
Check relevance
Show venue, date, topic, language and accessibility information.
Choose to attend
The person enrols and optionally enables programme reminders.
CARRY FORWARD
Selected venue or area and chosen programme; prefer manual area selection when sufficient.
KEEP SEPARATE
No background location tracking or attendance inference from prayer-tool use.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Daily tools create relevant discovery; local organisers reach interested participants.
SUCCESS: User-requested local discovery → suitable event enrolments → confirmed attendance.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 12 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A learner can choose a path from participation to contribution
Learning participation → Volunteer application  |  A learner who wants to give back
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“This helped me. I want to support others when I am ready.”
USE WHEN
Offer an optional volunteer path after the person expresses interest in contributing.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Learning progress, religiosity or aid receipt never creates an obligation to volunteer.
Interest in service
The learner chooses a suitable contribution area.
Relevant preparation
Show actual role expectations and optional or required preparation.
Apply and assess
Reuse consented profile details; complete separate volunteer checks.
Start within limits
Approved volunteers accept bounded work with coordinator support.
CARRY FORWARD
Selected interests, contact details and relevant assessed skills with consent.
KEEP SEPARATE
A certificate, course attendance or worship streak does not confer service authority.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Learners gain an achievable contribution route; MRM grows prepared, willing capacity.
SUCCESS: Interest → applications → approvals → sustained suitable service; watch burden and dropout.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 13 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
A volunteer can connect a person to the right specialist
Volunteer support → Specialist referral  |  A volunteer whose assigned case exceeds their remit
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“I can accompany this person, but their next need requires authorised expertise.”
USE WHEN
Route through MRM when a need exceeds the volunteer’s approved competence.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
The app never treats a teaching badge as legal, medical or financial accreditation.
Recognise a boundary
The volunteer records a minimal referral request on their authorised case.
Staff review
MRM checks consent, urgency and the appropriate referral pathway.
Approved handoff
Share necessary information with an authorised partner under policy.
Keep continuity
Track acknowledgement and next ownership; the volunteer sees permitted status.
CARRY FORWARD
Minimum agreed referral context, consent and case/reference ID to authorised recipients.
KEEP SEPARATE
No public case broadcast, unapproved partner access or assumption of specialist credentials.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
The seeker avoids repeating the story unnecessarily; the volunteer avoids unsafe overreach.
SUCCESS: Appropriate referrals → acknowledged handoffs → clear next owner and follow-up.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 14 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
Public discovery can continue into the same service journey
Website → App participation  |  A visitor reading a programme or volunteer opportunity
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“I want this exact programme, not to start again on a generic home screen.”
USE WHEN
Preserve the public destination across install, sign-in and eligibility checks where feasible.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Public information stays accessible; installation is not needed just to read it.
Specific public page
The visitor chooses a programme, volunteer role or support route.
Keep the destination
Carry a non-sensitive link or short reference through entry.
Required checks only
Sign in or apply when the selected action requires it.
Resume the action
Return to the same programme or application with current availability.
CARRY FORWARD
Public destination ID and safe campaign/source reference; no private case data in URLs.
KEEP SEPARATE
No secrets in deep links. Expired programmes receive an honest alternative.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Visitors keep their intent; MRM loses fewer people between discovery and participation.
SUCCESS: Destination retained → intended action completed; test installation and expired-link paths.
PROPOSED USER JOURNEY 15 / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
Service experience can guide a person’s next development step
Volunteer review → Learning development  |  A volunteer reflecting with a coordinator
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
“What did I do well, and what training would help me contribute better?”
USE WHEN
Use an agreed private review to recommend learning or future duties.
NOT REQUIRED WHEN
Do not convert volunteer hours or popularity into teaching approval or public expertise claims.
Review service
The volunteer and authorised coordinator reflect on a completed duty.
Agree development
Select a specific skill goal without copying beneficiary details.
Choose learning
Offer an approved course or mentor relevant to that goal.
Assess progression
Review learning and suitability before any new responsibility.
CARRY FORWARD
Agreed skill goal and restricted competency evidence; public recognition only by policy.
KEEP SEPARATE
No beneficiary story or private feedback on public profiles; no automatic teacher badge.
VALUE ON BOTH SIDES
Volunteers see a development path; MRM builds capacity with evidence rather than rank.
SUCCESS: Agreed plans → useful training → assessed competence; track wellbeing as well as retention.

Seeker journey: support can open a chosen learning path
Learning complements assistance when useful. It is never a condition for receiving help.
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
Ask for help
A seeker requests beginner Quran guidance.
Appropriate helper

Learn and follow up

Continue independently

SHARED PRODUCT RULES / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
Reuse helpful context; grant each role separately
One person can be a learner, teacher and volunteer. Each relationship still has its own approval and permissions.
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
ONE PERSON
Reuse an account and consented profile details. Do not create a new identity for every feature.
SEPARATE ROLES
Teacher approval, publishing entitlement and volunteer eligibility are independent states.
EXPLICIT RELATIONSHIPS
An enrolment, mentor acceptance, duty confirmation or case assignment gives a bounded relationship.
VISIBLE RELEVANCE
Show approved subject expertise and status on a support offer—not private learning or worship records.
CONTROLLED CONTEXT
Carry selected goals, public programme IDs or referral status. Record who consented to what.
SAFE EXIT AND RETURN
Decline, pause or leave the second journey without losing the original service; handle revoked roles.
DECISIONS AND ACCEPTANCE / MRM DIGITAL COMMUNITY PLATFORM
Validate that each bridge earns its place
Agree the product behaviour, then test it with the people who would actually cross between services.
MRM / ZYLAX TECHNOLOGIES
PROPOSED PRODUCT DESIGN · OPTIONAL PARTICIPATION · SEPARATE ROLE APPROVALS
PRODUCT DECISIONS
Confirm visible teacher credentials, volunteer checks, invitation timing, referral ownership and consent wording.
USER VALUE TEST
Can a teacher, volunteer or seeker explain why the suggested second service helps—and decline it easily?
MEANINGFUL FLOW TESTS
Declining keeps teaching available. Payment grants no case access. Revoked credentials stop appearing as current. Expired links recover honestly.
RECIPROCAL OUTCOME
Measure appropriate accepted handoffs and user-reported usefulness. Do not optimise pressure to enrol, volunteer or disclose.
A connected platform helps a person take the right next step for their goal.
